name: Bombay–Thane passenger railway
description: Passenger railway service connected Bombay and Thane under the Great Indian Peninsula Railway.

impact.note: One short line bringing an existing technology to India; the subcontinent's network grew from this start, but the record is the first line only.

places.note: Place refers to the sourced event; historic political boundaries are not inferred.

date.basis: Date stated in the cited source.

events.statement: An inaugural passenger train left Bori Bunder for Thane with about 400 guests and passengers.

evidence.supports: Indian Railways describes the 16 April 1853 Bombay–Thane inaugural run with fourteen carriages and about 400 guests and passengers, and the 1854 Howrah–Hooghly public line.

events.caveats: The inaugural trip does not establish the ticket conditions, class composition or ordinary daily traffic.

date.basis: Date stated in the cited source.

events.statement: An advertisement offered passenger journeys and class fares for a planned daily service beginning 18 April.

evidence.supports: The government magazine reproduces the passenger notice and class-based fares in rupees, annas and pies. It reproduces an offer, not proof of individual tickets sold.
The newspaper dates the reproduced public passenger advertisement to 8 April 1853 and quotes planned service beginning Monday the 18th; it does not establish actual service on that day.

events.caveats: The announcement is evidence of an offer, not actual transactions or proof of service on that day.

date.basis: Date of the opening for traffic as recorded in Danvers’s section table. The company’s first revenue period starts the same day. A contemporary press summary gives 17 April.

events.statement: The Government Director’s report records 18 April as the date the Bombay–Tannah section opened for traffic.

evidence.supports: The Government Director’s section-opening table dates Bombay to Tannah to 18 April 1853 in a row grouped with the Mahim branch and lists Tannah to Callian separately on 1 May 1854.

evidence.locator: Appendix No. 1, printed p. 292 (scan page 318), statement signed 15 June 1858
evidence.supports: The signed company revenue account begins its first period on 18 April 1853 and closes it on 30 June 1854, recording receipts, working expenses and net profits paid to the East India Company against interest advanced.

evidence.locator: 5 November 1853, vol. 11, no. 532, printed p. 1260 (scan page 24), Great Indian Peninsula
evidence.supports: The contemporary newspaper summary of the company directors’ eighth half-yearly report gives 17 April for opening Bombay to Tannah and reports two trains running daily thereafter. The directors’ original report was not inspected.
The reproduced advertisement set Monday 18 April as the planned start of daily passenger service.

events.caveats: The 8 April advertisement proposed daily passenger service from 18 April. The November 1853 press summary gives 17 April and reports daily trains thereafter. Company receipts cover a period that includes the Callian extension. The date of the first ordinary passenger train or ticket remains unresolved.

evidence.supports: The official opening table identifies the Bombay to Tannah section under the Great Indian Peninsula Railway.

evidence.locator: Appendix No. 1, printed p. 292 (scan page 318), statement signed 15 June 1858
evidence.supports: The signed company revenue account begins its first period on 18 April 1853 and closes it on 30 June 1854, recording receipts, working expenses and net profits paid to the East India Company against interest advanced.

earliest_record.rationale: The 8 April advertisement is the earliest dated public documentation here and gives the terms offered. The invitation run on 16 April and the reported opening for traffic on 18 April have separate events.

research.note: Independent review checked the previously recorded offer, inaugural event and measures. The reported traffic opening and operator contribution await review of the revised wording.

unresolved.note: The inspected account does not identify a specific represented locomotive as the design ancestor of this service.
